summary:
AgroAdapt AI is a web app that turns satellite and environmental data into plain farming advice, with a focus on Ethiopia.

What it does: you explore a 3D globe, search for a district or neighbourhood, and get a report for that area covering climate, vegetation, land cover, terrain, soil, and crops and advice.
Where the data comes from: open services that need no API key, including NASA GIBS (imagery), NASA POWER (climate from 1991 to 2025), MODIS (vegetation and land cover), NASADEM (terrain) and ISRIC SoilGrids (soil).
What makes it different: every result shows its evidence, including the source, method, confidence and limits. Your own soil-test results outrank the satellite estimates.
Crop advice: 16 crops are scored against FAO ECOCROP requirements and graded S1, S2, S3 or N, with the most limiting factor named.
How it’s built: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with a MapLibre globe, and no backend or login so far.

Status after three build rounds: the globe, map layers and the full Analyse section are built. They were tested with stand-in data only, so the calls to the live services still need checking in a real browser.

Still to do: fire history (needs a free FIRMS key), numeric colour legends, full translations, the Field Card and PDF report, and offline mode.
details:
AgroAdapt AI in more detail

Goal: make complex Earth-observation data usable by farmers, agricultural professionals, researchers and decision-makers, supporting productive and climate-resilient farming. The tagline is “Earth Intelligence. Smarter Agriculture.”

How a user moves through it

  1. The app opens on a 3D globe showing NASA satellite imagery.
  2. The user searches a district or neighbourhood, and the app loads its boundary from OpenStreetMap. If none is mapped, it uses a circle of 1, 2, 5 or 10 km.
  3. The user confirms the area (limit 2,500 km²).
  4. The app produces a report cut to that boundary, in eight tabs.

The eight report tabs

Tab

What it shows

Source

Overview

Key figures for the area

All sources below

Climate

Rain, temperature, soil wetness and solar, with the 1991–2020 baseline compared against 2021–2025 and trend tests

NASA POWER

Vegetation

25 months of NDVI greenness at 250 m, with cloud and snow removed

MODIS via ORNL DAAC

Land cover

Share of each land class, first year against latest

MODIS via ORNL DAAC

Terrain

Elevation and slope classes

NASADEM via OpenTopoData

Soil

Modelled soil properties at 0–30 cm and texture class

ISRIC SoilGrids

Survey

Your own field results: texture, pH, organic matter, depth, drainage, salinity, NPK

User input, saved in the browser

Crops & advice

Suitability of 16 crops and practical recommendations

FAO ECOCROP file

The ideas that set it apart

  • Evidence Trail: every result lists its provider, dates, method, confidence and limits.
  • Pixel Truth: the app shows how large one data pixel is next to a 2 ha field, so regional data isn’t mistaken for field-level data.
  • Adaptation Signal: recent seasons are compared with a 30-year baseline to show how the land is changing. It is planned as Milestone 6, and the Climate tab already makes this comparison.
  • Ground-Truth Loop: field measurements outrank satellite estimates.
  • Honesty rule: no invented data, and anything simulated must carry a “DEMO DATA” label.

Recommendations

Each one states the action, the reason, the evidence, the confidence and the limits. They cover soil sampling, crop choice, cereal–legume rotation, lime or alkalinity checks, water harvesting, dry spells, erosion on slopes of 10% or more, urban growth, and planting at rain onset.

Technology

  • Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no framework and no build step.
  • MapLibre GL JS serves as both the 3D globe and the flat map.
  • Charts are inline SVG, and data is saved in the browser’s local storage.
  • There is no backend, login or API key yet. A small backend is planned for when the FIRMS and Earthdata keys are added.

Progress

  • Round 1: covered in the first build log, which I haven’t opened in this conversation.
  • Round 2 (14 Nov): globe fixes and the first climate analysis.
  • Round 3 (15 Nov): the full Analyse section with all eight tabs, plus OpenFreeMap labels and street basemap.

Main open risk: everything was tested with stand-in replies, so the live services still need checking in a real browser.

Not built yet: fire counts, numeric colour legends, full translations (the analysis text is English only), the Field Card and PDF report, and offline mode.
